The texts an epoch circuit's builder follows first do not: V06 §3.7.1 (V06 l. 1479-1480: 'F-WALL's ladder (§5.2) binds the trace; a trace that fails it leaves the stage unwalled, the circuit re-evaluated at the next growth (reported)') and V06 §3.17 (3) (V06 l. 2496-2497) send it to F-WALL, whose detection names the raised-way meeting (l. 9855) while its ladder cell gives that meeting a rung only 'at generation, a regeneration and a village derivation' and a hand op none, the epoch unnamed; S5a's pin rule, which an epoch's new stage and contractWall run, ends 'that crossing takes F-WALL's raised-way rung' with no path (l. 6603). A builder may run the generation rung at an epoch (the band widened to wall.barrierReachM) or leave the stage unwalled with no walls.waited count. Both keep law 1; law 2 (c) decides the epoch's outcome and T110-2 (4)'s table-edit variant asserts it ('an epoch circuit across the standing aqueduct waiting (walls.waited)', l. 19490-19492), so a wrong build fails a named bar: a minor.
